task_description: A physics word-problem: compute the volume (in mL, rounded to nearest integer) occupied by 0.312 kg of Freon-12 (R-12, dichlorodifluoromethane) when sitting at the bottom of the Mariana Trench and allowed to stabilize at the Trench's 'peak' (highest) bottom temperature. The correct method must account for the extreme pressure (~1086 bar) compressing the liquid, raising its density well above the ~1-atm value; the gold answer is 55 mL, implying a compressed-liquid density of roughly 5670 kg/m3 (i.e., the team's value was off by ~4x). The expected answer represents the actual in-situ volume of the highly compressed Freon-12 at trench depth.
final_vs_expected: produced 225 vs gold 55 — team used ~1-atm saturated-liquid density (~1384 kg/m3) and ignored the ~1086 bar pressure compression that the gold answer requires (true density ~5670 kg/m3, ~4x denser)
primary_cause: Single-agent physics error: WebResearcher computed volume from the 1-atm saturated-liquid density of Freon-12 and never applied the trench's ~1086 bar pressure compression, and no one ever ran an actual equation-of-state / CoolProp computation despite having the lead.
mast_rationale: 1.1 (disobey task spec): the task hinges on the trench's ~1086 bar pressure, which the team explicitly noted (WebResearcher T1: 'pressure of 1,086 bar'; Analyst T2: 'around 1086 atm') yet computed volume from saturated/1-atm density anyway, dropping the constraint that defines the problem. 3.2 (no/incomplete verification): the Critic repeatedly demanded 'actual computation' but the Analyst never ran run_python and no equation-of-state lookup at 1086 bar was ever performed; the loop only re-checked arithmetic of 0.312/1384, not the physics. 3.3 (incorrect verification): the Critic's final-round acceptance ('the arithmetic is internally consistent', T7/T15) and the Finalizer's T19 endorsement validated an answer whose density input was physically wrong — verification theater that checked self-consistent arithmetic on an invalid premise. 1.5 (unaware of termination): the Finalizer waffled (T12 refused, T19 finalized) and the team burned 19 turns looping on the same '225' without ever resolving the open physics question before terminating on an unsupported answer.
trace_narrative: T1: Selector routes to WebResearcher, who searches trench temp (finds '1 to 4 C' and pressure '1,086 bar') and Freon-12 density sources, then in round-2 reasoning fixes density at 4 C ~1384 kg/m3 by interpolating Wikipedia table values and computes 0.312/1384 ~= 225 mL; publishes just '225' (no method, no sources). T2: Analyst privately muses density could be ~1.21 or ~1.39 g/mL, notes the 1086 atm pressure and that Freon-12 'is likely a compressed liquid at this pressure' — then drops that concern, back-solves 312/225 = 1.3867 g/mL, declares it 'plausible', and republishes '225'. T3: Critic (correctly) flags the bare '225' as unsupported, no posted computation or sources, asks WebResearcher for data and Analyst for the calculation. T4-T11: WebResearcher re-searches (even surfaces CoolProp R12 docs and the 200 MPa max-pressure note in T4, never used), repeatedly republishes '225' or a 1384 kg/m3 interpolation narrative; Analyst republishes '225' with the same 1-atm arithmetic. T7/T13/T15: Critic softens to 'plausible and internally consistent' but keeps asking for source excerpts and an explicit Analyst computation. T12: Finalizer refuses ('Need the WebResearcher/Analyst evidence...'). T14/T16: WebResearcher posts the cited Wikipedia values and interpolation. T18: Analyst again posts '225'. T19: Finalizer, deciding the source-backed values are 'probably enough', emits FINAL ANSWER: 225 — wrong, because the underlying density never accounted for pressure.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is fundamentally a single-agent capability failure that the team's verification structure failed to catch, not an inter-agent information-distortion failure. The root error is physics: the correct in-situ volume requires the density of Freon-12 as a compressed liquid at ~1086 bar, which is far higher than its ~1-atm saturated-liquid density of ~1384 kg/m3. The gold answer 55 mL implies ~5670 kg/m3, i.e., the liquid is compressed ~4x denser at trench pressure. The team had every clue: WebResearcher's very first search returned '1,086 bar' pressure, Analyst's reasoning explicitly said 'Freon-12 is likely a compressed liquid at this pressure', and WebResearcher's T4 search surfaced the CoolProp R12 page (which lists max pressure 200 MPa and could give the exact density at 1086 bar). Yet nobody ever evaluated density at that pressure; they collapsed onto saturated-liquid density at 4 C and only ever re-verified the trivial arithmetic 0.312/1384. The secondary failure is verification theater: the Critic correctly insisted on 'actual computation' but only ever scrutinized whether the posted arithmetic was self-consistent, never whether the chosen density was physically appropriate for 1086 bar — so a self-consistent-but-wrong premise passed. The Analyst, the agent with run_python, NEVER executed code in any of its 4 turns; it just pattern-matched '225' and back-justified it. Structurally the run also wasted ~10 turns looping (T4-T18) re-posting '225' without advancing the physics, and the Finalizer flip-flopped (T12 refuse, T19 accept) on unchanged evidence.
reasoning_vs_published: The most telling private-vs-published gap is Analyst T2: privately it noted the decisive physics — 'Freon-12 is likely a compressed liquid at this pressure, with a possible density around 1.39 g/mL' and 'significant pressure—around 1086 atm' — recognizing pressure matters, but then abandoned it, back-solved 312/225=1.3867 g/mL to rationalize the incoming number, and published only '225'. This is reasoning-action drift toward confirmation rather than info distortion: it didn't hide a correct answer, it talked itself out of the right concern. WebResearcher T5 privately wavered ('The earlier answer of 225 mL seems off... 223 mL makes more sense' and 'the pressure effect might complicate matters') yet published the clean 1384 kg/m3 / 225 mL story with no mention of the pressure caveat — a genuine but minor communication-loss / unreflective-publishing instance: the private doubt about pressure never reached the team. The Critic's reasoning shows the false-trust mechanism: T7 'I can't independently verify the Wikipedia values without tools' and T15 'I'm wondering if I should accept the user's statement regardless' — it knew it lacked verification capability and ultimately let plausibility substitute for it. The Finalizer T19 reasoning is the clearest verification-theater tell: 'The critic's last note mentioned still being unsupported... Is everything resolved? It's probably enough to finalize' — finalizing on an explicitly-still-unsupported answer. Crucially, no agent ever privately reasoned the correct (pressure-corrected) answer, so there was no right answer being withheld — the team was uniformly wrong, which is why genuine inter-agent misalignment is only weak.
